data.name: ack
data.value: I understand the risk and want to continue

data.name: ai_def
data.value: Name a game (CS2, Apex, Fortnite, Dota 2, Warzone, CoD, LoL, PUBG, Valorant) or ask about risks, profile, RAM.

data.name: ai_hi
data.value: I'm a local AI advisor. In the demo answers are rule-based; the C# version will plug in a local model. Tell me which game to optimize for (CS2, Apex, Fortnite, Dota 2, Warzone, CoD, LoL, PUBG, Valorant), or ask about risks and RAM. I reply in the language of your question.

data.name: ai_ok
data.value: No red-zone settings; the configuration is balanced.

data.name: ai_ram
data.value: Open the “RAM timings” tab: it has three overclock levels for your kit.

data.name: bk_d
data.value: Created on first launch, before any change. Stored in the app folder until you delete it yourself: you can return to the original settings at any time, even after closing the app or rebooting the PC.

data.name: bk_none
data.value: No backup. The app will create one on next launch from the current PC state.

data.name: bk_opened
data.value: The app will open the backup folder (demo)

data.name: bk_un
data.value: When uninstalling, the installer offers to restore the original settings first.

data.name: d_background
data.value: What runs next to the game and eats resources

data.name: d_hardware
data.value: Detected hardware, clocks and profile match

data.name: d_network
data.value: Latency and connection stability in online games

data.name: d_ramt
data.value: Approximate BIOS speeds and timings: mild, medium and strong overclock

data.name: d_system
data.value: Power plan, Game Mode and Windows priorities

data.name: h_cfg
data.value: Demo PC configuration (auto-detected in the app)

data.name: lap_bios
data.value: Usually not available in a laptop BIOS

data.name: lap_ram
data.value: Laptops often lock memory settings and use SO-DIMM, so these values may be unavailable. Do not force them.

data.name: ov.gaincap
data.value: Expected FPS gain from active settings. Effects partly overlap, so the upper bound does not exceed 20%.

data.name: ov.intro
data.value: System status, ready-made profiles and safety. A profile sets the starting values; you can then fine-tune everything manually in the sections.

data.name: pl_d
data.value: Corvite adapts its limits and risk scales to your device.

data.name: pl_lapd
data.value: Laptop: stricter limits and its own risk scale

data.name: pl_pcd
data.value: Desktop: full limits, depends on your cooling

data.name: prof.game.sub
data.value: Balance of response, FPS and temperature

data.name: prof.max.sub
data.value: Limit of your cooling, red zone

data.name: proto
data.value: PROTOTYPE: nothing is applied to your PC

data.name: r_note
data.value: Values are approximate (~). Change them in BIOS manually and verify stability (TestMem5, MemTest86). The app applies nothing.

data.name: r_over
data.value: Above kit rating, depends on silicon lottery

data.name: rz1
data.value: These values exceed the safe range for most systems. They raise temperature and power load; crashes and reboots are possible.

data.name: rz2
data.value: A restore point is created before applying. Settings roll back automatically on overheating.

data.name: tip.foot
data.value: Estimate for a typical gaming system. Values are approximate (~).

data.name: tip.sliderwarn
data.value: The green part of the scale is safe for most systems. The red part needs good cooling and can cause crashes.

data.name: tw.aggr.desc
data.value: The higher the value, the more often memory is cleared. Clearing too often forces the game to re-read data from disk.

data.name: tw.aggr.sub
data.value: How often to flush the cache

data.name: tw.antil.desc
data.value: The driver synchronizes CPU and GPU so frames are queued later. Latency is lower. Compatibility depends on the game.

data.name: tw.bgcap.desc
data.value: Limits background processes while a game runs. Too strict a limit will slow antivirus and cloud sync.

data.name: tw.bgcap.sub
data.value: How much CPU background processes may use

data.name: tw.boost.desc
data.value: Raises the clock ceiling in single-core loads. Above a certain value the CPU stops being stable.

data.name: tw.boost.sub
data.value: Shift of the maximum core clock

data.name: tw.co.desc
data.value: Lowers core voltage at the same clock: less heat, higher boost. Too strong an offset causes errors at idle.

data.name: tw.dns.desc
data.value: Speeds up resolving the game server address when connecting. Does not affect in-match latency.

data.name: tw.dns.sub
data.value: Public DNS instead of your ISP's DNS

data.name: tw.dvr.desc
data.value: Stops constant background video recording. Frees some GPU and disk resources.

data.name: tw.dvr.note
data.value: Clips through Game Bar will stop being recorded.

data.name: tw.dvr.sub
data.value: Less load on GPU and disk

data.name: tw.fast.desc
data.value: Fast Startup keeps part of the system state between boots, which lets driver faults accumulate.

data.name: tw.focus.desc
data.value: Turns on focus mode. Notification windows do not minimize the game or cause hangs.

data.name: tw.focus.sub
data.value: No pop-up windows over the game

data.name: tw.fso.desc
data.value: Turns off Windows overlay processing for fullscreen games, which reduces frame output latency.

data.name: tw.g_reg.desc
data.value: The app remembers the original value of every setting. Any tweak can be returned to factory state in one click.

data.name: tw.g_reg.sub
data.value: Old values are kept for the "Restore all" button

data.name: tw.g_rest.desc
data.value: A Windows restore point is created before every apply so the system can be restored.

data.name: tw.g_roll.desc
data.value: If CPU or GPU temperature exceeds the threshold, the app restores the last safe settings.

data.name: tw.g_roll.sub
data.value: Settings revert if the threshold is exceeded

data.name: tw.g_temp.desc
data.value: The temperature at which the rollback triggers. Keep it below your hardware's factory throttling limit.

data.name: tw.g_temp.sub
data.value: Higher value, later the protection triggers

data.name: tw.gamemode.desc
data.value: Windows gives the game more CPU time and does not start driver updates while you play.

data.name: tw.gamemode.sub
data.value: Priority to the game, fewer background tasks

data.name: tw.gcore.desc
data.value: Adds a fixed value to the core clock. Near the maximum the risk of artifacts and driver crashes grows.

data.name: tw.gmem.desc
data.value: Increases video memory bandwidth. Helps at high resolutions. Memory errors can lower FPS without obvious crashes.

data.name: tw.gpm.desc
data.value: Switches the driver power mode. The clock does not drop between scenes, so frametime is smoother.

data.name: tw.gpm.sub
data.value: GPU does not lower clocks at idle

data.name: tw.gpow.desc
data.value: The GPU holds its maximum clock longer until it hits the power limit.

data.name: tw.gpow.sub
data.value: Upper power draw limit in watts

data.name: tw.gtemp.desc
data.value: Defines when the GPU starts dropping clocks because of heat. High values require good case airflow.

data.name: tw.gtemp.sub
data.value: Temperature up to which boost is allowed

data.name: tw.hags.desc
data.value: Takes some work off the CPU. The effect depends on the game and driver: sometimes a gain, sometimes a small loss of up to −2%.

data.name: tw.hags.sub
data.value: The GPU manages its own frame queue

data.name: tw.idx.desc
data.value: During a game the search indexer does not touch the disk or load the CPU.

data.name: tw.idx.sub
data.value: Windows Search does not read the disk

data.name: tw.kill.desc
data.value: Closes selected programs (messengers, browsers, sync) and restores them after the game.

data.name: tw.kill.name
data.value: Close background apps when a game starts

data.name: tw.kill.note
data.value: Unsaved data in the programs being closed may be lost.

data.name: tw.lowlat.desc
data.value: The driver keeps the frame queue minimal. Mouse and keyboard input responds faster, especially in GPU-bound games.

data.name: tw.lowlat.sub
data.value: Shorter frame queue between CPU and GPU

data.name: tw.minst.desc
data.value: The higher the value, the higher the clock stays even without load. Response is better, but idle temperature and power draw rise.

data.name: tw.nagle.desc
data.value: Windows stops merging small packets. For TCP games this lowers response latency.

data.name: tw.nagle.sub
data.value: Packets are sent immediately, without batching

data.name: tw.nthr.desc
data.value: Windows limits packet processing speed during multimedia playback. This setting removes the limit.

data.name: tw.park.desc
data.value: Windows stops "sleeping" unused cores. Games get resources without a wake-up delay.

data.name: tw.pbo.desc
data.value: Raises the board's power and current limits for boost. Needs a board with good power delivery and a cooler.

data.name: tw.pl2.desc
data.value: Lets the CPU hold its peak clock longer. K-series chips need a strong cooler, otherwise they throttle.

data.name: tw.plan.desc
data.value: Enables the hidden Ultimate Performance power plan. The CPU and buses never enter power-saving states, so response in games is smoother.

data.name: tw.plan.note
data.value: On a laptop it will shorten battery life.

data.name: tw.plan.sub
data.value: CPU does not drop its clock at idle

data.name: tw.ppt.desc
data.value: Lets the CPU hold a high clock longer under load. Needs a good cooler and a board with strong power delivery.

data.name: tw.ppt.sub
data.value: How many watts the CPU can sustain

data.name: tw.prio.desc
data.value: The game gets cores before background programs. "Realtime" can block input and disk, so the app does not recommend going above "High".

data.name: tw.refl.desc
data.value: Enables Reflex where the game supports it. The frame queue is shorter, response is faster.

data.name: tw.refl.name
data.value: NVIDIA Reflex (if the game supports it)

data.name: tw.shader.desc
data.value: Increases the amount of stored shaders. Reduces stutter when effects first appear in a game.

data.name: tw.standby.desc
data.value: When the standby memory list grows, games start to hang. The app flushes it when a threshold is reached.

data.name: tw.standby.stab
data.value: Fewer freezes with 16 GB or less

data.name: tw.standby.sub
data.value: Frees the cache that has filled RAM

data.name: tw.sysmain.desc
data.value: The service preloads programs into memory. It helps little on an SSD, while the disk load remains.

data.name: tw.sysmain.note
data.value: Recommended for SSD only. Leave it on for HDD.

data.name: tw.tcpauto.desc
data.value: Restores the safe TCP window sizing mode. Helps with odd speed drops.

data.name: tw.telem.desc
data.value: Reduces the diagnostic data Windows sends in the background. Applied via policies; services are not removed.

data.name: tw.timer.desc
data.value: Reduces the system timer step. Games stumble less often for no reason, but the PC wakes from idle more often.

data.name: tw.tlim.desc
data.value: The higher the limit, the later the CPU starts lowering its clock. Constantly running near the upper limit shortens lifespan.

data.name: tw.tlim.sub
data.value: Temperature at which clocks start dropping

data.name: tw.tmp.desc
data.value: Before a game starts, removes safe Windows and browser temporary files.

data.name: tw.tmp.sub
data.value: Frees space and speeds up disk access

data.name: tw.trim.desc
data.value: Regularly tells the SSD which blocks are free. Write speed does not degrade over time.

data.name: tw.upd.desc
data.value: While a game is running, Windows Update does not download or install packages.

data.name: tw.uvi.desc
data.value: Reduces voltage: less heat and more time at high boost. Too large a value causes crashes.

data.name: tw.vfx.desc
data.value: Disables window animations and transparency. Only noticeable on weak GPUs and integrated graphics.

data.name: undo_t
data.value: State before the last apply restored. Undo steps left:

data.name: unsup
data.value: Intel GPUs are not supported yet: section disabled.

data.name: wl_d
data.value: Laptops have limited cooling and power delivery, and their components are often power-limited by the manufacturer. Heavy overclocking can cause overheating, throttling, battery wear or permanent damage, and may void the warranty. For laptops Corvite narrows the sliders and uses a stricter risk scale. Keep the charger connected, watch temperatures and avoid the red zone.

data.name: wp_d
data.value: Changing system and hardware settings can cause instability, overheating, crashes, data loss or a shorter component lifespan. Corvite saves a backup of your original settings and can roll everything back, but it cannot guarantee safety on every PC. Overclocking is at your own risk.

data.name: planned
data.value: This section arrives in a later development stage (see TZ, section 15). The shell and navigation are already in place.

data.name: unsup_gpu
data.value: Intel GPUs are not supported yet: section disabled.

data.name: pl_auto
data.value: Type detected automatically. Please check and confirm.

data.name: pl_mm_risk
data.value: Your device was detected as a laptop, but you selected PC mode. Overclocking in this mode is done at your own risk and is intended for experienced users only: a laptop has limited cooling and power, so overheating, throttling and hardware damage are possible.

data.name: pl_mm_info
data.value: Your device was detected as a PC, but you selected Laptop mode. This is safe, but the overclocking limits will be cut roughly in half.

data.name: tool.note
data.value: Corvite does not download or install anything by itself. The link opens the manufacturer's site and the rest is up to you. Many laptops lock these settings in the BIOS, in which case they will not work even with the program.

data.name: tool.none
data.value: There is no official program for this setting yet, or it is still in development

data.name: tool.xtu.why
data.value: Intel CPU power limits and clocks are changed at a low level, which Corvite cannot do itself yet. Intel's official utility lets you set them manually. It has no command-line interface, so it cannot be built into Corvite.

data.name: tool.rm.why
data.value: AMD CPU power limits, Curve Optimizer and PBO are changed at a low level, which Corvite cannot do itself yet. AMD's official utility lets you set them manually. I found no command-line interface for it, so it cannot be built into Corvite.

data.name: tool.nvdrv.why
data.value: Corvite controls the GPU power limit and clocks through NVML, a library installed with the NVIDIA driver. If the driver is missing or outdated, the setting is unavailable. Install a current driver from NVIDIA's site.

data.name: tool.nvprof.why
data.value: This setting lives in the NVIDIA driver profile and there is no public interface to change it. Set it manually in the NVIDIA app or NVIDIA Control Panel, which come with the driver.

data.name: tool.amdgpu.why
data.value: Radeon settings live in the AMD driver, and Corvite does not use a public interface for them yet. Set them manually in AMD Software: Adrenalin Edition, installed with the driver.
